 Absentee voting underway for Dec. 1 runoff elections in parts of Pine Belt 
 Absentee voting underway for Dec. 1 runoff elections in parts of Pine Belt. By Quentis Jones Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 7:48 PM CST | Updated : 17 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PINE BELT, Miss. (WDAM) - Voters in parts of the Pine Belt are preparing to head back to the polls as absentee voting gets underway for the Dec. 1 runoff elections.
 Several local races remain undecided following the Nov. 3 general election, including a judicial contest and a county supervisor’s race.
 In Chancery Court District 13, Place 2, candidates George Schmidt and John Smallwood are facing off after neither received enough votes to win outright in November.
 The district includes Forrest, Perry and Stone counties.
 Covington County voters in Supervisor District 2 will also return to the polls to choose between Gary Deen and Robert Aultman.
 Forrest County Circuit Clerk Gwen Wilks said voters should understand Mississippi’s absentee voting requirements before attempting to cast a ballot.
 Unlike states that allow no-excuse early voting, Mississippi requires voters to meet specific eligibility requirements to vote absentee. Those who qualify can cast an absentee ballot in person at their county circuit clerk’s office or, under certain circumstances, by mail.
 The deadline to vote absentee in person for the Dec. 1 runoff is Saturday, Nov. 28. Circuit clerk offices will be open from 8 a.m. until noon that day.
 Another election scheduled for December
 Some Pine Belt voters will also have another opportunity to cast a ballot later in the month.
 A special election is scheduled for Dec. 22 to fill the Mississippi Senate District 34 seat left vacant by former state Sen. Juan Barnett.
 The district includes portions of Forrest, Jones and Jasper counties.
 Six candidates are seeking the seat, including former Hattiesburg Mayor Johnny DuPree.
 If no candidate receives a majority of the votes, a runoff election is scheduled for Jan. 19, 2027.
 Election officials encourage residents to check which races appear on their ballots and become familiar with absentee voting requirements and deadlines.
 Voters can contact their county circuit clerk’s office or visit the Mississippi Secretary of State’s website at www.sos.ms.gov for additional election information.
